name: Iron Pillar of Delhi
description: A 7.2m rust-resistant iron pillar with Brahmi inscriptions. Citations: Balasubramaniam, R. (2005), 'Story of the Delhi Iron Pillar'; Upinder Singh (2006), 'Delhi: Ancient History to the Present'.

name: Rock Edict of Ashoka (Srinivaspuri)
description: An in-situ Minor Rock Edict carved into quartzite detailing Ashoka's Dhamma teachings. Citations: Upinder Singh (2006), 'Delhi: Ancient History to the Present'; Romila Thapar (1961), 'Asoka and the Decline of the Mauryas'.

name: Ashokan Pillar (Feroz Shah Kotla)
description: Monolithic sandstone pillar brought from Topra in 1356 CE by Feroz Shah Tughlaq. Citations: Shams-i Siraj 'Afif, 'Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi'; Upinder Singh (2006), 'Delhi: Ancient History to the Present'.

name: Ashokan Pillar (Northern Ridge)
description: Monolithic sandstone pillar brought from Meerut and re-erected on the Northern Ridge. Citations: Catherine B. Asher (1992), 'Architecture of Mughal India'; Upinder Singh (2006), 'Delhi: Ancient History to the Present'.

name: Anangtal Baoli
description: An 11th-century masonry step-well built by Tomar king Anangpal II in Lal Kot. Citations: B.R. Mani (1997), 'Excavations at Lal Kot 1991-92 and Beyond'; Upinder Singh (2006), 'Delhi: Ancient History to the Present'.

name: Lal Kot & Wall of Kila Rai Pithora
description: Massive stone fortification walls defining the early medieval city of Delhi. Citations: Y.D. Sharma (1974), 'Delhi and its Neighbourhood (ASI)'; Cynthia Talbot (2015), 'The Last Hindu Emperor: Prithviraj Chauhan'.

name: Qutb Minar Complex
description: Includes the 73m victory minaret, Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque, and iron pillar. Citations: J.A. Page (1926), 'An Historical Memoir on the Qutb: Delhi (ASI)'; Percy Brown (1942), 'Indian Architecture: Islamic Period'.

name: Tomb of Iltutmish
description: Square sandstone mausoleum with Arabic calligraphy and geometric carvings. Citations: Catherine B. Asher (1992), 'Architecture of Mughal India'; Y.D. Sharma (1974), 'Delhi and its Neighbourhood (ASI)'.

name: Sultan Ghari
description: India's earliest Islamic mausoleum, built as an underground crypt for Prince Nasiruddin Mahmud. Citations: S.A.A. Rizvi (1987), 'The Wonder That Was India Vol. II'; Y.D. Sharma (1974), 'Delhi and its Neighbourhood (ASI)'.

name: Balban's Tomb
description: Historical ruin containing the earliest true arch and dome in Indian Islamic architecture. Citations: Percy Brown (1942), 'Indian Architecture: Islamic Period'; Y.D. Sharma (1974), 'Delhi and its Neighbourhood (ASI)'.

name: Alai Darwaza & Alai Minar
description: Red sandstone gateway with marble inlay and the base of an ambitious unfinished giant minaret. Citations: Percy Brown (1942), 'Indian Architecture: Islamic Period'; J.A. Page (1926), 'An Historical Memoir on the Qutb (ASI)'.

name: Siri Fort Remains (Shahpur Jat)
description: Rubble fortification walls of Delhi’s second medieval city built to repel Mongol invasions. Citations: Peter Jackson (1999), 'The Delhi Sultanate: A Political and Military History'; Y.D. Sharma (1974), 'Delhi and its Neighbourhood (ASI)'.

name: Chor Minar
description: Stone tower with 225 holes used to display severed heads of executed Mongol prisoners. Citations: R.V. Smith (2005), 'The Delhi That No-one Knows'; Y.D. Sharma (1974), 'Delhi and its Neighbourhood (ASI)'.

name: Tughlaqabad Fort
description: Colossal stone fortress with massive bastions housing the third city of Delhi. Citations: Anthony Welch & Howard Crane (1983), 'The Tughluqs: Master Builders of the Delhi Sultanate'; Y.D. Sharma (1974), 'Delhi and its Neighbourhood (ASI)'.

name: Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq's Tomb
description: Pentagonal fortress tomb made of red sandstone with a white marble dome. Citations: Anthony Welch (1983), 'The Tughluqs: Master Builders of the Delhi Sultanate'; Percy Brown (1942), 'Indian Architecture: Islamic Period'.

name: Adilabad Fort
description: Citadel south of Tughlaqabad built in heavy-rubble architectural style. Citations: Y.D. Sharma (1974), 'Delhi and its Neighbourhood (ASI)'; Tatsuro Yamamoto et al. (1967), 'Delhi: Architectural Remains of the Delhi Sultanate Period'.

name: Bijay Mandal & Ramparts
description: Remains of a palace structure believed to be the 'Palace of Thousand Pillars' in Jahanpanah. Citations: H. Suroor (2011), 'Delhi: 1000 Years of Building'; Y.D. Sharma (1974), 'Delhi and its Neighbourhood (ASI)'.

name: Begumpur Mosque
description: Massive multi-domed congregational mosque serving Jahanpanah. Citations: Anthony Welch (1983), 'The Tughluqs: Master Builders of the Delhi Sultanate'; Matsuo Ara (1982), 'The Historical Monuments of the Delhi Sultanate'.

name: Khirki Mosque
description: Roofed fortress-style mosque with latticed windows (khirki) and grid courtyards. Citations: Anthony Welch (1983), 'The Tughluqs: Master Builders of the Delhi Sultanate'; Lucy Peck (2005), 'Delhi: A Thousand Years of Building'.

name: Satpula
description: Seven-arched stone dam and water gate built into the wall of Jahanpanah. Citations: Lucy Peck (2005), 'Delhi: A Thousand Years of Building'; Y.D. Sharma (1974), 'Delhi and its Neighbourhood (ASI)'.

name: Hauz Khas Complex & Feroz Shah Tomb
description: Islamic seminary, mosque, and L-shaped tomb complex built around a reservoir. Citations: Sayyid Ahmad Khan (1847), 'Asar-us-Sanadid'; Anthony Welch (1983), 'The Tughluqs: Master Builders of the Delhi Sultanate'.

name: Feroz Shah Kotla
description: Citadel of Firozabad with palace ruins, grand mosque, and an Ashokan pillar. Citations: Shams-i Siraj 'Afif, 'Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi'; Lucy Peck (2005), 'Delhi: A Thousand Years of Building'.

name: Kalu Sarai Mosque
description: Partially ruined neighborhood mosque in Malviya Nagar with plaster-coated domes. Citations: Y.D. Sharma (1974), 'Delhi and its Neighbourhood (ASI)'; Lucy Peck (2005), 'Delhi: A Thousand Years of Building'.

name: Tomb of Mubarak Shah
description: Octagonal royal mausoleum with an arcade and sloping buttresses. Citations: Percy Brown (1942), 'Indian Architecture: Islamic Period'; Y.D. Sharma (1974), 'Delhi and its Neighbourhood (ASI)'.

name: Mohammad Shah's Tomb
description: Classic octagonal tomb in Lodi Gardens adorned with chhatris and tiles. Citations: Catherine B. Asher (1992), 'Architecture of Mughal India'; Y.D. Sharma (1974), 'Delhi and its Neighbourhood (ASI)'.

name: Bahlol Lodi's Tomb
description: Multi-domed sandstone structure built for the founder of the Lodi Dynasty. Citations: Sayyid Ahmad Khan (1847), 'Asar-us-Sanadid'; Y.D. Sharma (1974), 'Delhi and its Neighbourhood (ASI)'.

name: Sikandar Lodi's Tomb
description: Octagonal tomb set in a walled garden, precursor to Mughal double-dome layout. Citations: Percy Brown (1942), 'Indian Architecture: Islamic Period'; Lucy Peck (2005), 'Delhi: A Thousand Years of Building'.

name: Bara Gumbad & Mosque
description: Large domed gateway attached to a richly decorated three-bay mosque in Lodi Gardens. Citations: Y.D. Sharma (1974), 'Delhi and its Neighbourhood (ASI)'; Lucy Peck (2005), 'Delhi: A Thousand Years of Building'.

name: Moth-ki-Masjid
description: Signature Lodi mosque with sandstone and plaster filigree. Citations: Sayyid Ahmad Khan (1847), 'Asar-us-Sanadid'; Percy Brown (1942), 'Indian Architecture: Islamic Period'.

name: Rajon ki Baoli
description: Elaborate three-storey stepwell with attached mosque and tomb in Mehrauli. Citations: Y.D. Sharma (1974), 'Delhi and its Neighbourhood (ASI)'; Lucy Peck (2005), 'Delhi: A Thousand Years of Building'.

name: Dadi-Poti & Biran Gumbads
description: Cluster of prominent Lodi-era domed tombs in Green Park / Hauz Khas. Citations: Y.D. Sharma (1974), 'Delhi and its Neighbourhood (ASI)'; Lucy Peck (2005), 'Delhi: A Thousand Years of Building'.

name: Purana Qila (Old Fort)
description: Massive stone fortifications built on the historic mound of Indraprastha. Citations: M.C. Joshi (1993), 'Excavations at Purana Qila'; Catherine B. Asher (1992), 'Architecture of Mughal India'.

name: Qila-i-Kuhna Mosque
description: Transitional mosque in Purana Qila showcasing pointed arches and marble inlay. Citations: Percy Brown (1942), 'Indian Architecture: Islamic Period'; Catherine B. Asher (1992), 'Architecture of Mughal India'.

name: Isa Khan's Tomb & Mosque
description: Octagonal tomb enclosure predating Humayun’s Tomb, inside the complex. Citations: Catherine B. Asher (1992), 'Architecture of Mughal India'; Y.D. Sharma (1974), 'Delhi and its Neighbourhood (ASI)'.

name: Salimgarh Fort
description: Island fortress on the Yamuna, later converted into a state prison. Citations: Y.D. Sharma (1974), 'Delhi and its Neighbourhood (ASI)'; Swapna Liddle (2011), 'Chandni Chowk: The Shopkeeper's Delight'.

name: Sher Mandal
description: Octagonal red sandstone tower used as an observatory and library by Humayun. Citations: Catherine B. Asher (1992), 'Architecture of Mughal India'; Y.D. Sharma (1974), 'Delhi and its Neighbourhood (ASI)'.

name: Humayun's Tomb
description: UNESCO site; first garden-tomb on the Indian subcontinent. Citations: Glenn D. Lowry (1987), 'Humayun's Tomb: Form, Function, and Meaning in Early Mughal Architecture'; Ebba Koch (2002), 'Mughal Architecture'.

name: Arab ki Serai Gateway
description: Monumental entrance to the courtyard that housed Persian craftsmen for Humayun's Tomb. Citations: Catherine B. Asher (1992), 'Architecture of Mughal India'; AKTC Report (2010), 'Humayun's Tomb Urban Renewal Project'.

name: Afsarwala Tomb & Mosque
description: Located inside Humayun's Tomb complex; octagonal tomb on raised platform. Citations: Y.D. Sharma (1974), 'Delhi and its Neighbourhood (ASI)'; Lucy Peck (2005), 'Delhi: A Thousand Years of Building'.

name: Ataga Khan's Tomb
description: Decorated marble and sandstone tomb in Nizamuddin built for Akbar's prime minister. Citations: Ebba Koch (2002), 'Mughal Architecture'; Y.D. Sharma (1974), 'Delhi and its Neighbourhood (ASI)'.

name: Tomb of Khan-i-Khanan (Abdul Rahim)
description: Built for his wife and later his own resting place; stripped for Safdarjung's Tomb. Citations: Allison Busch (2011), 'Poetry of Kings: The Classical Hindi Literature of Mughal India'; AKTC Conservation Document (2020).

name: Red Fort (Lal Qila)
description: Imperial palace fortress of red sandstone forming Shahjahanabad's core. Citations: Ebba Koch (2001), 'The Complete Taj Mahal and the Riverfront Gardens of Agra/Delhi'; Gordon Sanderson (1914), 'The Red Fort, Delhi: Archaeological Survey of India Memoir'.

name: Jama Masjid
description: One of India's largest congregational mosques, built with red sandstone and white marble. Citations: Catherine B. Asher (1992), 'Architecture of Mughal India'; Stephe Blake (1991), 'Shahjahanabad: The Sovereign City in Mughal India'.

name: Roshanara Bagh & Tomb
description: Vast Mughal garden surrounding the open-air pavilion tomb of Princess Roshanara. Citations: Ebba Koch (2002), 'Mughal Architecture'; Swapna Liddle (2018), 'Delhi: 14 Historic Walks'.

name: Shalimar Bagh (Sheesh Mahal)
description: Royal country palace and garden where Aurangzeb crowned himself emperor in 1658. Citations: Stephen Blake (1991), 'Shahjahanabad: The Sovereign City in Mughal India'; Y.D. Sharma (1974), 'Delhi and its Neighbourhood (ASI)'.

name: Moti Masjid (Red Fort)
description: Small three-domed private mosque built entirely in white marble inside Red Fort. Citations: Ebba Koch (2002), 'Mughal Architecture'; Catherine B. Asher (1992), 'Architecture of Mughal India'.

name: Chaunsath Khamba
description: Unique hall constructed entirely of white marble with 64 pillars in Nizamuddin. Citations: Y.D. Sharma (1974), 'Delhi and its Neighbourhood (ASI)'; Lucy Peck (2005), 'Delhi: A Thousand Years of Building'.

name: Barapullah Bridge
description: 11-arched stone bridge spanning the Kushak Nallah near Nizamuddin. Citations: Lucy Peck (2005), 'Delhi: A Thousand Years of Building'; Y.D. Sharma (1974), 'Delhi and its Neighbourhood (ASI)'.

name: Chini ka Rauza (Delhi)
description: Small tomb in Nizamuddin decorated with Persian glazed tilework (chini). Citations: Y.D. Sharma (1974), 'Delhi and its Neighbourhood (ASI)'; Lucy Peck (2005), 'Delhi: A Thousand Years of Building'.

name: Badli-ki-Serai Ruins
description: Historic traveler resting house on GT Road, later site of 1857 battle. Citations: William Dalrymple (2006), 'The Last Mughal'; Y.D. Sharma (1974), 'Delhi and its Neighbourhood (ASI)'.

name: Jamali Kamali Mosque & Tomb
description: Sandstone mosque and tomb adorned with colorful tiles and Persian verses. Citations: Karen Toshima (2002), 'Sufi Shrines of Delhi'; Y.D. Sharma (1974), 'Delhi and its Neighbourhood (ASI)'.

name: Nila Gumbad & Sabz Burj
description: Early Mughal tombs featuring glazed blue and green Timurid tilework. Citations: Ebba Koch (2002), 'Mughal Architecture'; ASI Monograph (2019), 'Humayun's Tomb Conservation Project'.

name: Zeenat-ul-Masajid (Ghata Masjid)
description: Riverside mosque in Daryaganj built on high plinth with black-white striped domes. Citations: Stephen Blake (1991), 'Shahjahanabad: The Sovereign City in Mughal India'; Catherine B. Asher (1992), 'Architecture of Mughal India'.

name: Fakhr-ul-Masajid
description: Ornate red sandstone and marble mosque in Kashmiri Gate built in 1728. Citations: Sayyid Ahmad Khan (1847), 'Asar-us-Sanadid'; Swapna Liddle (2011), 'Chandni Chowk: The Shopkeeper's Delight'.

name: Tripolia Gates
description: Two triple-arched brick and stone gateways standing on GT Road in Rana Pratap Bagh. Citations: Y.D. Sharma (1974), 'Delhi and its Neighbourhood (ASI)'; Lucy Peck (2005), 'Delhi: A Thousand Years of Building'.

name: Sunehri Masjid (Chandni Chowk)
description: Gilded three-domed mosque where Nadir Shah directed the 1739 massacre. Citations: William Dalrymple (2006), 'The Last Mughal'; Stephen Blake (1991), 'Shahjahanabad: The Sovereign City in Mughal India'.

name: Qudsia Bagh & Mosque
description: Former royal pleasure garden and palace complex north of the old city wall. Citations: Swapna Liddle (2018), 'Delhi: 14 Historic Walks'; Y.D. Sharma (1974), 'Delhi and its Neighbourhood (ASI)'.

name: Sunehri Masjid (Red Fort)
description: Located near Delhi Gate of Red Fort with gilded copper domes. Citations: Catherine B. Asher (1992), 'Architecture of Mughal India'; Y.D. Sharma (1974), 'Delhi and its Neighbourhood (ASI)'.

name: Safdarjung's Tomb
description: Last garden-tomb of Mughal style built for the Vizier of Emperor Ahmad Shah. Citations: Catherine B. Asher (1992), 'Architecture of Mughal India'; Percy Brown (1942), 'Indian Architecture: Islamic Period'.

name: Sunehri Masjid (Sardar Patel Marg)
description: Gilded-dome neighborhood mosque near modern Central Vista. Citations: Y.D. Sharma (1974), 'Delhi and its Neighbourhood (ASI)'; Lucy Peck (2005), 'Delhi: A Thousand Years of Building'.

name: Zafar Mahal & Moti Masjid
description: Final summer palace built by the last Mughal Emperor Bahadur Shah Zafar in Mehrauli. Citations: William Dalrymple (2006), 'The Last Mughal'; Swapna Liddle (2018), 'Delhi: 14 Historic Walks'.

name: Hijron ka Khanqah
description: Spiritual retreat in Mehrauli containing graves dedicated to transgender individuals. Citations: Karen Toshima (2002), 'Sufi Shrines of Delhi'; Y.D. Sharma (1974), 'Delhi and its Neighbourhood (ASI)'.

name: Gandhak ki Baoli
description: Delhi's oldest operational step-well in Mehrauli named after sulfurous water. Citations: Y.D. Sharma (1974), 'Delhi and its Neighbourhood (ASI)'; Lucy Peck (2005), 'Delhi: A Thousand Years of Building'.

name: St. James' Church
description: One of Delhi's oldest churches, built in Renaissance Neo-Classical cross layout. Citations: William Dalrymple (2006), 'The Last Mughal'; Swapna Liddle (2018), 'Delhi: 14 Historic Walks'.

name: Mutiny Memorial (Ajitgarh)
description: Gothic spire on Northern Ridge commemorating soldiers from the 1857 siege. Citations: William Dalrymple (2006), 'The Last Mughal'; Christopher Hibbert (1978), 'The Great Mutiny: India 1857'.

name: Coronation Park Site
description: Open ground used for three Imperial Durbars (1877, 1903, 1911). Citations: Robert Irving (1981), 'Indian Summer: Lutyens, Baker, and Imperial Delhi'; Narayani Gupta (1981), 'Delhi Between Two Empires 1803-1931'.

name: Rashtrapati Bhavan
description: Originally Viceroy's House; Neo-Classical palace with Buddhist/Indian motifs. Citations: Robert Irving (1981), 'Indian Summer: Lutyens, Baker, and Imperial Delhi'; Christopher Hussey (1950), 'The Life of Sir Edwin Lutyens'.

name: Parliament House (Old)
description: Colonnaded circular sandstone building inspired by Chausath Yogini Temple. Citations: Robert Irving (1981), 'Indian Summer: Lutyens, Baker, and Imperial Delhi'; Narayani Gupta (1981), 'Delhi Between Two Empires'.

name: India Gate
description: 42m-high war memorial arch honoring Commonwealth soldiers from WWI. Citations: Robert Irving (1981), 'Indian Summer: Lutyens, Baker, and Imperial Delhi'; Gavin Stamp (2002), 'The Memorial to the Missing of the Somme'.
